title: Berkeley fully depleted CCD fabrication and characterization

questions.reason: The 1996 designers cite Holland's 1989 paper at the phosphorus-doped polysilicon gettering step and describe removal of the thick getter before applying a transparent contact. The 1997 reports and Holland's patent add technical detail with overlapping authorship. Spieler participated in the 1990 preamplifier work and discusses the broader lineage. Independent confirmation of the exact process on the December 1996 on-sky prototype is still missing.

Holland cites Hu and describes the same deposited backside polysilicon impurity sink, with in-situ phosphorus doping and an additional electrical role. The link records a shared principle. Direct influence of IBM's specific process remains unresolved.

The 1996 prototype report and 1997 characterization, which share authors, both identify the 1987 Lick data acquisition system. The design abstract and a separate 1987 photometer report document the named system's readout arrangement. The relation is scoped to the laboratory.

findings: Hu's 1977 IBM-assigned patent reports experiments on integrated circuit test structures with a deposited backside polysilicon impurity sink. Holland's 1989 article cites Hu and describes the same principle in high-resistivity silicon p-i-n diodes.

Chen and Silvestri report a separate experiment using backside polysilicon after epitaxial growth. They cite Hu and acknowledge discussions with him. This supports the technique family and has the IBM affiliation in common.

The 1996 prototype paper cites the 1989 fabrication study directly at its description of the phosphorus-doped polysilicon getter. It reports removing the thick getter for backside illumination. Holland's later patent describes the same approach to depositing a thin optical window.

The 1996 prototype paper §4 and ref. [12] and the 1997 Lick characterization §3.2 and ref. [3] identify the earlier Lick data acquisition system used in lab tests. The 1997 report describes double-correlated amplification and 16-bit digitization.
frontier: Find the 1996 prototype's fabrication traveler or Microsystems Laboratory process sheets to identify which getter steps were run and when the thick layer was replaced by the transparent contact.

Trace Spieler's two intermediate steps using Holland and Spieler's LBL-28667 report, Holland's 1992 IEEE paper on high-resistivity CMOS and the laboratory records behind the 1997 Holland, Wang and Moses photodiode paper.

Compare Lauer's 1981 PDP-8 manual and the 1987 UNIX system paper against instrument installation notes and dated Lick manuals to identify the earlier system components that survived the computer/software transition.

screen: Searched discovery and source text, lead IDs and record aliases for Lick readout, CCD data acquisition, Hu, gettering, high-resistivity silicon and diode fabrication. Extended the existing Berkeley records. The IBM process and UNIX-era Lick system have no matching records or leads. The earlier Lauer PDP-8 configuration is a frontier question.
limits: Robinson's 1987 paper was accessible as its abstract and publication metadata. The system link is confined to lab characterization. The IBM patent gives a dated disclosure and test descriptions. Absolute priority and direct transfer to Berkeley remain unresolved.
